..summary: instanceSelectionError and restrictedSendViolationError are structurally identical custom error types with duplicated Error(), nil-check, and reason-code patterns

evidence: instance_selector.go:14-38 — instanceSelectionError with message+reasonCode fields and nil-safe Error()
send_restriction_policy.go:31-55 — restrictedSendViolationError with identical structure and identical nil-check pattern
Both have parallel asXxxWithReason() helper functions doing errors.As + reason extraction
detail.suggestion: Extract a single policyError struct (message, reasonCode) in helpers.go with a generic asPolicyError() accessor. Reduces duplication and standardizes policy-violation error handling

..summary: JSONB (map[string]interface{}) used as domain model forces 800+ lines of manual type-assertion parsing in handlers instead of typed structs

evidence: send_restriction_policy.go:77-138 — readSendRestrictionsSettings performs 30+ type assertions against JSONB map to build a typed struct
JSONB is map[string]interface{} so every consumer must type-assert at runtime with no compile-time safety
Three nearly identical Value()/Scan()/GormDBDataType() implementations across JSONB, JSONBArray, StringArray (~80 lines of duplication)
detail.suggestion: Introduce typed settings structs (e.g., SendRestrictionSettings, OrganizationSettings) with a single JSONB marshal/unmarshal point. The GORM Value()/Scan() duplication across JSONB/JSONBArray/StringArray can be eliminated with a generic JSONWrapper[T] type

..summary: Handlers bypass MessageProvider abstraction by checking isWhatsmeowProvider() and using WhatsApp client directly

evidence: stubs.go:63-80 — MarkMessageRead checks isWhatsmeowProvider(), calls MessageProvider.MarkRead() for whatsmeow path but calls a.WhatsApp.MarkMessageRead() for Meta path, bypassing the interface
ProviderGuard reads config directly (a.Config.WhatsApp.Provider) instead of checking provider capabilities through the interface
detail.suggestion: Ensure all message operations route through the MessageProvider interface. Add MarkRead/MarkMessageRead to the interface contract, or introduce a ProviderCapabilities query method so handlers don't need to know which concrete provider is active

..summary: Identical config validation calls duplicated in runServer — ValidateDatabaseCredentials and ValidateWebhookVerifyToken each called twice

evidence: Lines 178-179: config.ValidateDatabaseCredentials(cfg) + Fatal
Lines 183-184: config.ValidateWebhookVerifyToken(cfg) + Fatal
Lines 188-189: config.ValidateDatabaseCredentials(cfg) + Fatal (exact duplicate)
Lines 191-192: config.ValidateWebhookVerifyToken(cfg) + Fatal (exact duplicate)
detail.suggestion: Remove the duplicate calls at lines 188-193, keeping only the first set at lines 178-184

..summary: Dead no-op RBAC middleware block in setupRoutes that only checks OPTIONS then returns, with a comment saying permission checks moved to handlers

evidence: Lines 1283-1294: g.Before() callback that checks for OPTIONS method then returns r unconditionally with comment 'Route-level permission checks are now handled at the handler level'
detail.suggestion: Remove the dead middleware block — it adds no behavior and is leftover scaffold

..summary: DELETE responses use 3 different shapes: {message: 'X deleted'}, {message: 'X deleted successfully'}, {status: 'deleted'}

evidence: instances.go:406 returns {"status": "deleted"}
accounts.go:335 returns {"message": "Account deleted successfully"}
canned_responses.go:304 returns {"message": "Canned response deleted"} (no 'successfully')
conversation_notes.go:271 returns {"message": "Note deleted"} (no 'successfully')
detail.suggestion: Standardize DELETE responses to a single shape: either {"message": "<Resource> deleted"} or 204 No Content. Pick one convention and apply uniformly.

..summary: /api/campaigns/{id}/progress and /api/campaigns/{id} map to the same GetCampaign handler, and /api/chats maps to ListContacts

evidence: main.go:1445: g.GET("/api/campaigns/{id}", app.GetCampaign)
main.go:1452: g.GET("/api/campaigns/{id}/progress", app.GetCampaign) — identical handler
main.go:1340: g.GET("/api/contacts", app.ListContacts)
main.go:1356: g.GET("/api/chats", app.ListContacts) — returns contacts-shaped response under /api/chats
detail.suggestion: Either create a dedicated GetCampaignProgress handler returning only progress fields, or remove the /progress route. For /api/chats, either create a dedicated handler or document the alias explicitly in the frontend contract.

..summary: List endpoints return inconsistent pagination metadata — accounts, instances, and organizations omit total/page/limit

evidence: accounts.go:80 returns SendEnvelope(map[string]interface{}{"accounts": response}) with no total/page/limit
instances.go:215 returns SendEnvelope(instances) — bare array with no pagination wrapper
organization.go returns SendEnvelope(map[string]any{"organizations": response}) with no total/page/limit
Compare with campaigns.go:157, contacts.go:858, users.go, teams.go, tags.go which all include total/page/limit
detail.suggestion: Standardize all list endpoints to include {resource_name: [...], total: int, page: int, limit: int} envelope. Add parsePagination calls to accounts.go, instances.go, and organization.go list handlers.

..summary: ReadyCheck uses raw integer 500 instead of fasthttp.StatusInternalServerError constant

evidence: app.go:90: SendErrorEnvelope(500, "Database connection error", nil, "")
app.go:93: SendErrorEnvelope(500, "Database ping failed", nil, "")
app.go:98: SendErrorEnvelope(500, "Redis connection error", nil, "")
362 other calls across the codebase correctly use fasthttp.StatusInternalServerError
detail.suggestion: Replace raw 500 with fasthttp.StatusInternalServerError in app.go:90,93,98

..summary: meta_analytics.go uses raw string literals 'analytics'/'read'/'write' instead of models.ResourceAnalytics constant

evidence: Line 52: a.HasPermission(userID, "analytics", "read", orgID) instead of models.ResourceAnalytics
Line 355: a.HasPermission(userID, "analytics", "read", orgID) — same raw string
Line 392: a.HasPermission(userID, "analytics", "write", orgID) — same raw string
All other handlers (widgets, chat_close_ratings, etc.) use models.ResourceAnalytics constant
detail.suggestion: Replace raw "analytics" strings with models.ResourceAnalytics in all three locations in meta_analytics.go
